verification.summary: JIF Barracuda was struck by two projectiles northeast of Khor Fakkan on 18 October. One crew member suffered minor injuries; the tug continued its voyage.

audit_notes: IMO confirms name, IMO, date, position and one injured. Maritime Executive identifies vessel type and describes projectiles. Imported mine/tanker attribution is unsupported for this named vessel. No vessel-wide death count is stated.

verification.summary: Singapore’s MPA reports that GFS Pride was struck by an unknown projectile on 13 October, caught fire and sank. All 21 crew were safely evacuated; no injuries were reported.

sources.source: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore

verification.date_note: Attack date as reported by Singapore MPA in Singapore Time; no UTC event time was supplied.

audit_notes: MPA explicitly gives date in Singapore Time, not UTC. Keep date precision day and do not invent UTC midnight. MPA supports zero deaths/injuries at report time through all crew safely evacuated. No nationalities of dead applicable; no Singaporeans aboard does not identify crew nationalities.

verification.summary: Wine Trader caught fire off Sulina on 15 October. Later reporting quotes its manager describing a drone attack and seven crew still missing: six Beninese and one Russian national. Missing crew are not counted as confirmed deaths.

sources.source: Romanian Naval Authority — initial rescue statement

Original Maritime.bg manager interview https://www.maritime.bg/156457/ linked by TürkiyeToday returned429.

verification.summary: Maritime reporting citing MSCIO describes a small craft firing at a containership north of Bab el-Mandeb on 7 October; security consultants identify CUL Klang. The crew was reported uninjured and the ship continued north.
verification.location_text: North of Bab el-Mandeb, southern Red Sea

audit_notes: Both full articles opened: exact attack7Oct; later article publication9Oct. Feed8Oct reference appears publication/report date, not second attack. Source names security consultants as hull identification; MSCIO is quoted but underlying advisory not read. Reported incident confidence, not direct official named confirmation. Do not infer Chinese crew nationality from AIS broadcast as independently confirmed; no crew count in sources.
